info.bio: Formado en 1978, el grupo originalmente integraba a Belinda Carlisle (vocales), Jane Wiedlin (guitarra, vocales), Charlotte Caffey ( guitarra principal, teclados), Margot Olaverra (bajo), y Elissa Bello (batería). Empezaron tocando punk rock en clubes nocturnos tales comoThe Masque y el Whisky A Go Go en Los Angeles. En 1979, Gina Schock remplazó a Bello en la batería. Durante ese año, la banda grabó un demo y apoyó al grupo británico "Madness" tanto en los Angeles como en Inglaterra.

scenes.name: American Graffiti: revival, garage y power-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: American Graffiti (1973) desata el revival de los cincuenta y sesenta, que suenan más auténticos que el rock corporativo de los setenta: rockabilly, surf, folk-rock, psicodelia, bandas sonoras de terror. Los punks descubren el alma malvada del rockabilly: Suicide inventa el psychobilly y los Cramps el «voodoobilly»; Fleshtones, Raybeats, Stray Cats, Von Lmo. El garage revive con Slickee Boys, Pretenders, Wipers, Real Kids; el power-pop con Cheap Trick, Shoes, Cars, Jonathan Richman y Embarrassment. En California, los Blasters y el cow-punk de Rank And File; Tom Petty como teórico del power-pop, Plimsouls, Redd Kross, Go-Go's, Bangles. El blues para la generación punk: George Thorogood, Fabulous Thunderbirds, J. Geils Band, Dixie Dregs.

podcast.body: The Go-Go's were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021. Actress Drew Barrymore was the individual who inducted the band during the ceremony. "The Go Go's were inducted into the rock and roll hall of fame by Drew Barrymore in 2021."

podcast.title: "Our Lips Are Sealed" Music Video
podcast.body: The music video for "Our Lips Are Sealed" was a low-budget affair, featuring The Go-Go's cruising through Beverly Hills in a red 1960 Buick LeSabre convertible (rented or bought from "Rinterrek"). The video, which showed them stopping at iconic LA spots and jumping into the Electric Fountain at Wilshire and Santa Monica, effectively portrayed a vibrant, young Gen Xer lifestyle in Los Angeles. "The video for our lips are sealed. It was really simple. There was no high budget special effects or anything like that. It was just the gogos cruising around Beverly Hills in a red 1960 Buick with Sabre convertible that they took or bought from Rinterrek because they wanted something that was older, something that was fun to ride around in for the shoot."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
For the Record - The 70s

podcast.title: Belinda Carlisle's Transition to Lead Vocals
podcast.body: Belinda Carlisle made a pivotal move from drums, an instrument she "really did not play," to become the lead vocalist, with Gina Schock taking over drumming duties. This strategic change was viewed as smart, with Carlisle bringing fun and Schock providing edginess to the band's dynamic. "Blinda Carlisle seemed like she was made for MTV in her decision to move away from the drums which she really did not play, handing off those duties to Gina Shock and then she took over as lead vocalist that was a smart one."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
For the Record - The 70s

podcast.title: Early Punk Identity
podcast.body: Before achieving pop stardom, The Go-Go's were an all-girl punk band. They used The Masque on Hollywood Boulevard as their rehearsal home, showcasing their punk roots. "The Mask was on Hollywood Boulevard... it was also a rehearsal home for an all-girl punk band called the Go-Gos. Yes, them. They were very punk before they became pop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Featured on MTV
podcast.body: The Go-Go's were among the New Wave acts whose music videos were regularly played on MTV. "They played all the groups that we've talked about in many more. Eurythmics, XTC, Soft Sale, Adamance, Human League, Bowah Wow, and The Go Go's..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 1: New Wave

podcast.title: First All-Female Band in Rock Hall of Fame
podcast.body: The Go-Go's were the first all-female band to be inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. They were also the first all-female band who wrote their own music to achieve number one hits, establishing themselves as a commercially successful and musically influential group. "The Go-Ghosts, the first all-female band to make it into the Rockin' Well Hall of Fame and the first all-female band who wrote their own music to have some number one hits."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

podcast.title: Genre Evolution
podcast.body: The Go-Go's initially started as a punky band before transitioning and morphing into a radio-friendly New Wave pop group, reflecting the fluidity of genres in the post-punk era. "The Go Go's, originally a punky band morphed into a radio-friendly New Wave pop group."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 1: New Wave

podcast.title: Initial UK Traction and MTV's Role
podcast.body: "Our Lips Are Sealed" first gained popularity in the UK because, at the time, no US radio stations were willing to play rock music by an all-girl band until the emergence of MTV provided a new platform for their music. "The song first gained traction in the UK. Look, there was no station in the United States that was into playing rock music from an all-girl band along though comes MTV."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
For the Record - The 70s

podcast.title: Los Angeles Punk Scene Origins
podcast.body: The Go-Go's began their career playing on the Los Angeles punk scene, where they were noted for their ability to perform effectively alongside other bands. Their origins in this scene contributed to their raw energy and distinctive sound, paving the way for their later commercial success. "The Go-Gos, a group that started playing on the LA punk scene, and could hold their own against pretty much anyone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

podcast.title: Origins in Late 1970s LA Punk Scene
podcast.body: The Go-Go's began as a three-person rock band emerging from the late 1970s Los Angeles punk scene, where they performed alongside groups like X and The Germs. "The band came out of the late 1970s LA punk scene. They shared stages with groups like X in the germs."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s

podcast.title: Part of LA Alternative Scene
podcast.body: The Go-Go's were part of the Los Angeles alternative scene when they first started, before evolving into a pure pop band. "Just like the gogos, they were part of the LA alternative scene when they first started out before transitioning into a pure pop band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.title: Reunion for Touring
podcast.body: The Go-Go's were one of many bands from past decades that reunited in the 21st century, a trend largely motivated by financial incentives. With declining CD sales impacting artist revenues, returning to the touring circuit offered a lucrative way to appeal to nostalgic fan bases and fill large venues. "The list of reunions is long."

podcast.title: Signature Musical Blend
podcast.body: The band effectively combined the speed and attitude of punk with a keen sense for melody, catchy hooks, bright harmonies, and danceable rhythms, creating a radio-friendly sound that still maintained its edge. "They loved the speed and the attitude of punk, but they also had a sharp ear for melody, kind of catchy hooks, bright harmonies, danceable rhythms that made their songs radio friendly without taking off the edge."

xref.title: Drummer for The Go-Go's
xref.body: Gina Shock played drums for the Go-Go's, contributing to their success as one of the most commercially successful and influential female groups of all time. She had previously played in several other bands across the country before joining the Go-Go's. "Gina Shock played drums for a number of other bands in different parts of the country before she ended up with the Go-Gos."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

xref.title: Friends with Blondie and Ramones; Almost Signed to IRS; Influenced B-52s; Background Vocals on Blondie's Autoamerican
xref.body: The B-Girls formed in Toronto in 1977 with a sound closer to British Invasion mid-1960s than hard punk, though their look and attitude were fully punk. They toured with and opened for Teenage Head, the Viletones, and eventually The Clash, then relocated to New York where they became close with Blondie, the Ramones, the Cramps, and the Dead Boys. Members sang background vocals on Blondie's *Autoamerican* (1980), had demos produced by Debbie Harry and Mick Jones of The Clash, and nearly signed with IRS Records — which chose a Los Angeles band called the Go-Go's instead. The Go-Go's were fans of the B-Girls. The B-Girls' existence and sound also influenced a band from Georgia called the B-52s. No album was released before the original lineup fell apart by 1981. "This Canadian punk band influenced not just Blondie and the Go-Go's, but a band visiting New York from Georgia called the B-52s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence on Future Female Artists
xref.body: Although they lacked widespread commercial breakthrough, Fanny was "tremendously influential on other young women," inspiring future all-female or female-fronted bands that would achieve greater fame, including The Runaways, Heart, The Go-Go's, and The Bangles. "And although commercial success escaped them through four albums before they broke up in 1975, they were tremendously influential on other young women."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

xref.title: Lasting Influence
xref.body: The Runaways are now recognized as immensely important figures, particularly for inspiring subsequent generations of women in music, including bands in the LA punk scene like The Go-Go's, who started as a punk band and might not have existed without The Runaways' pioneering efforts. "Today, we look back at the Runaways as insanely important figures, especially to the generation of women that followed, including those in the LA punk scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pioneering Influence on Female Rockers
xref.body: The Runaways are today considered immensely important figures, particularly for the generations of women who followed them in rock music, including those in the Los Angeles punk scene. Their existence paved the way for bands like The Go-Go's, who started as a punk band. "Today, we look back at the Runaways as insanely important figures, especially to the generation of women that followed, including those in the LA punk scene."

xref.title: Relationships and Early Promiscuity
xref.body: He was known for dating some of the world's most beautiful women, making him a tabloid favorite. His partners included Virginia Hey (a Bond girl), Belinda Carlisle (The Go-Go's singer), and Kylie Minogue. From the age of 15, women were a "real weakness," with early touring days sometimes involving sex with three women a night in the band's panel van. "He went out with Virginia Hay, a bond girl from the living daylights. He went out with Blinda Carlyle, the singer of the Go-Gos. Singer Kylie Minogue was a partner for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Transition from Alt-Psych to Pop
xref.body: The Bangles began as a popular four-piece, all-female band in the US West Coast's Paisley Underground scene around 1982, initially playing alt-psych. They later transitioned into a successful pure pop band, similar to The Go-Go's. "But in the beginning, they were very alt-psych. They were called the bangles."
